title: I didn’t declare my crypto in previous years
excerpt: How to regularise past tax years before the Spanish Tax Agency (AEAT) acts first, which surcharges apply depending on when you do it, and why filing yourself isn’t the same as waiting to be asked.

hero.h1: You traded crypto and didn’t declare it
hero.subheading: It may be from two years ago or from five. Perhaps you didn’t know it had to be declared, or you left it for later. Only one thing matters now: if you file it yourself before they come asking, the cost is very different.

sections.body:
You bought crypto years ago, traded, perhaps sold. Nobody told you that swapping one token for another was taxable even if you never cashed out into euros, or you took it for granted until you read otherwise. You may even have declared the latest tax year correctly and realised, in doing so, that the earlier ones don’t add up.

The situation is more common than it seems, and there is an orderly way out. The tax authorities draw a sharp distinction between people who come forward and people who wait to be contacted. That distinction isn’t about how you’re treated: it’s about money.

What doesn’t make sense is to sit still and wait to see whether anything happens. With the automatic exchange of information between exchanges and tax administrations, the cross-check no longer depends on someone reviewing your file by hand.

sections.h2: Filing yourself versus waiting to be asked
sections.entrada: The tax itself is the same money, but the end result is nothing alike.

items: A supplementary return for the tax year is filed, on your own initiative
A late-filing surcharge applies, which increases with the time that has passed
There is no penalty, precisely because there has been no prior request from the tax authorities
You control the timing and the order in which the tax years are filed
The matter is closed with your figures and your approach documented

columnas.titulo: Waiting for the request to arrive
items: The tax authorities open the procedure and set the pace
Late-payment interest is added to the tax due
It opens the door to penalty proceedings, which run separately
The assessment is based on the data the AEAT has, not on yours
Challenging that assessment still means rebuilding your transactions, but against the clock

sections.entrada: The late-filing surcharge, when there has been no prior request, increases with the time that has passed since the filing deadline ended. These are the orders of magnitude; the exact calculation depends on your case.

steps.title: We rebuild from the very beginning, not from the year you want to declare
steps.body: Without the earlier history there is no reliable acquisition cost, and without an acquisition cost the gain comes out inflated. We start from your first purchase, even if that year is already time-barred.

steps.title: We establish which tax years are still open and which are time-barred
steps.body: Not everything old needs to be regularised. We calculate the statute of limitations on the actual dates of your case and tell you what is in and what isn’t.

steps.title: We quantify year by year
steps.body: How much tax is due in each year and which surcharge applies depending on the date it’s filed. You’ll see the total cost before deciding anything.

steps.title: You decide with the figures in front of you
steps.body: We explain the options and their consequences, including the unfavourable ones. The decision to regularise is yours, and it’s best made on an informed basis, not in a panic.

steps.title: We file the supplementary returns
steps.body: In the right order and with the supporting documentation on file, in case any tax year is reviewed later.

bullets: All the history you have, from your first purchase: exchange CSV files, read-only API keys, public wallet addresses.
The returns you did file for the tax years involved.
Bank statements showing money moving into and out of euros, which are often the only solid evidence for the older periods.
Whatever you remember about platforms that no longer exist: sign-up emails, old screenshots — any trace helps.
If you’ve received anything from the AEAT, the full notification. It changes the strategy completely.

items.q: Won’t regularising put me on their radar?
items.a: It’s the most common fear, and it’s worth looking at the other way round: with the automatic exchange of information, the AEAT already has, or will have, the exchange’s data. Regularising doesn’t put you on a radar you’re already on; what it does is get you there first, without a penalty and with your own figures.

items.q: How many years back do I need to go?
items.a: As a general rule, the tax authorities’ right to assess becomes time-barred four years after the end of the filing deadline, and the period is interrupted by any notified action. That said, to calculate the acquisition cost properly you have to rebuild from the beginning, including time-barred years: rebuilding is not the same as declaring.

That’s normal for older activity. It’s rebuilt from what does exist: the on-chain trail of your wallets, bank statements for purchases and sales against euros, confirmation emails. It doesn’t always get to one hundred per cent, but it does reach a documented position, and that is what gets defended.

Deferral and payment of tax debts in instalments are available and are requested through the usual channels. If the resulting amount is high, it’s best to raise it from the outset rather than when payment is already due.

items.q: Is it worth it if the tax due will be small?
items.a: Almost always, yes, because the problem is rarely that year’s tax: it’s that, without regularising, you carry a miscalculated acquisition cost into every following year. You either pay for it once or pay for it every year.

cierre.h2: The sooner you look at it, the less it costs
cierre.body: Tell us when you started trading, on which platforms and which tax years you think are undeclared. We’ll tell you what is time-barred, what needs regularising and how much it would cost to do it now compared with six months from now.
